cohort: The study included 5,309 American women aged >=20 years from the 2011-2018 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES).
finding: A higher android to gynoid (A/G) ratio was independently associated with an increased risk of stress urinary incontinence (SUI) in women aged >=20 years.
mod_finding: The number of vaginal deliveries and cesarean deliveries were found to potentially interact with the A/G ratio in relation to SUI.
